title: Dify vs n8n: Features, Pricing and Use Cases (2026)
summary: Dify vs n8n serve different purposes: Dify powers AI chatbots and document retrieval, while n8n automates workflows with distinct limits and pricing.
body_markdown:
## Activepieces as a third option for cross-app agents


Only one kind of job makes Activepieces worth a look: an AI agent that acts across many business apps, waits for a person to approve, and may need to run on your own servers.


Its MIT-licensed core can be self-hosted, and its agent step can reach any of its 741 integrations, so you probably don't need to build custom connectors.


Otherwise, the choice between Dify and n8n already covers you.


### When a third option is worth a look


Picture the request that lands on your desk on a Monday. "Can the agent read new support emails, check the order in our billing system, draft a refund, and ask me before sending it?"


That's not a chat app and not a RAG product. It's a task that crosses several tools, and a human has to say yes before money moves.


If that's your job, the comparison below is the quick check. It shows where each of the three tools fits, so you can see whether Activepieces adds anything beyond the two you're already weighing.


Best fit Open source status AI agent across integrations Human approval Self-hosting


Dify Building the AI app itself: chat, RAG, agents Open source Agents sit inside the app you build Not its core design Yes


n8n Moving data between many business apps, AI as one step Source-available, not fully open source AI steps within workflows Possible inside workflows Yes


Activepieces Agents acting across business apps Open source, MIT-licensed core AI agent step works across its 741 integrations Built into flows Yes


Read the table by row, not by column. Dify wins when the app is the product. n8n wins when the workflow is.


Activepieces, with 741 integrations under an MIT-licensed core, only enters if the agent, not the pipeline, is your center of gravity, which means pipeline-centric teams won't find it suitable.


### What Activepieces does differently


Activepieces has an MIT-licensed core and 741 integrations, which it calls[pieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces) , and its AI agent step can use any of them.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) puts the agent in the same flow as the fixed-rule steps, so your Monday request is one flow rather than an agent framework bridged to a workflow tool by a webhook.


Place an Agent step beside a plain step in the flow builder and the run trace logs a single execution from the support email to the refund, with approval as another step before the risky action.


You can also host it yourself when data must stay in your own environment. MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it in production.


It doesn't replace Dify's app-building. If you need a knowledge base, a chat front end, and prompt iteration, stay with Dify.


If the cross-app agent sounds like your Monday request, you can[try it free](https://cloud.activepieces.com/sign-up?ap_cta=blog_body&ref=%2Fblog%2Fdify-vs-n8n-features-pricing-and-use-cases-2026) .


For a team whose agent has to read support emails, check a billing system, draft a refund and pause for a person's approval, Activepieces is the better fit, judged on whether that whole job can live in one place.


An Agent step sits beside a deterministic automation step in the same flow, and the run trace logs one execution from start to finish, rather than two products bridged by a webhook and a callback.


If your agent doesn't span many apps, wait on human approval, or need to run on your own servers, the Dify-or-n8n choice still covers you.
